title: Sort Vowels by Frequency
summary: Given a string of lowercase English characters, rearrange only the vowels to appear in non-increasing order of their frequency.
statement: Given a string of lowercase English characters, rearrange only the vowels to appear in non-increasing order of their frequency. If vowels have the same frequency, order them by their first occurrence in the string. Return the modified string. Vowels include 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', and 'u', and their frequency is the count of their occurrences in the string.
constraints: Only vowel positions may change; consonants remain fixed.
Group vowels by decreasing total frequency.
Break equal-frequency ties by the vowel’s first occurrence in s.
hints: Count each vowel and record where it first appears.
Sort distinct vowels by negative frequency then first index.
Expand the ordered groups into a stream.
Replace only vowel positions from that stream, leaving consonants untouched.
editorial: Replace only vowel positions from that stream, leaving consonants untouched.

tests.explanation: e occurs three times and o once, so the vowel positions become e,e,e,o and the result is leetcedo.
The tied vowels a and a form the only vowel group, so the string is unchanged.
